paper.title: Bandits with Partially Observable Confounded Data

settings.name_in_paper: Linear Contextual Bandits with Linear Side Information
unmapped: K arms each with its own unknown parameter vector w_a in R^d (disjoint linear contextual model), reward <x_t, w_{a_t}> + eta_t
learner knows linear side information M_a w_a^* = b_a with M_a of rank L for each arm
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t \in [T]$ the environment outputs a context $x_t \in \X \subseteq \R^d$ sampled from some unknown distribution $\mathcal{P}_x$. ... the learner observes a reward $r_t = \inner{x_t, w^*_{a_t}} + \eta_t$ ... Assume we are given linear side information $M_{a} w^*_{a} = b_{a}$ ... $M_{a}, b_{a}$ are known

settings.name_in_paper: Linear contextual bandits with partially observable confounded offline data
unmapped: K arms each with its own unknown parameter vector w_a in R^d (disjoint linear contextual model)

access to an infinite offline dataset generated by a behaviour policy pi_b in which only the first L covariates of the context are observed (confounded); learner knows b_a^LS, R_11(a) and P^{pi_b}(a) from the data
learner can query the behaviour policy pi_b online (sample a ~ pi_b(x_t)) to estimate the cross-correlation R_12(a) at rate g(d,L)/sqrt(t) (Assumption 1)
settings.definition_quote: we assume a dataset ${\D = \brk[c]*{Q x_i, a_i, r_i}_{i=1}^N}$, in which $\brk[c]*{x_i}_{i=1}^N$ are i.i.d. samples from $\mathcal{P}_x$, $\brk[c]*{a_i}_{i=1}^N$ were generated by some fixed behavior policy, denoted by $\pi_b$ ... we assume only the first $L$ features of $x_i$ are visible in the data.

algorithms.name: OFUL with Partially Observable Offline Data

symbols.L_obs: rank L of the linear side information (number of observed covariates in the offline data)

conditions: ||P_a x|| <= S_{x,o} a.s. and ||P_a w_a^*|| <= S_{w,o}
tuning: sqrt(beta_t) = lam^{1/2} S_{w,o} + sigma sqrt((d-L) log(K(1+t S_{x,o}^2/lam)/delta))

source.label: thm: regret bound oful
source.quote: For all $T\geq 0$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, the regret of Algorithm~\ref{algo: projected oful} is bounded by $Regret{T}\leq \Olog\br*{(d-L)\sqrt{KT}}$.

results.notes: Regret defined on realized contexts via means; high probability w.r.t. noise. Proof gives explicit 2 sqrt(t) beta_t^{1/2} sqrt((d-L)K log(...)) bound.

bound.expression: 3*sqrt(T*(d - L_obs)*K*log(lam + T*L_feat**2/(d - L_obs)))*((sigma + L_feat*S*f_B1)*sqrt((d - L_obs)*log((1 + T*L_feat**2/lam)/(delta/(2*K*log(T))))) + sqrt(lam)*S) + (d - L_obs)*sqrt(K)*L_feat*S*f_B2

symbols.L_obs: number of observed covariates L in the offline data
symbols.f_B1: estimation-difficulty factor: max_a lambda_min(R_11(a))^{-1}/P^{pi_b}(a) * S_x (tr R_11 tr R_22)^{1/4} (up to log factors)
symbols.f_B2: max_a lambda_min(R_11(a))^{-1}/P^{pi_b}(a) * S_x^2 (up to log factors)

conditions: learner can query pi_b to estimate R_12(a) (Assumption 1)
tuning: sqrt(beta_{n,t}) = lam^{1/2} S_w + (sigma + S_x S_w f_n) sqrt((d-L) log((1+t S_x^2/lam)/(delta/(2 K log T))))
